subject: armadillo
pitch: A nine-banded armadillo trotting along. A shell of overlapping banded plates in dusty pinkish-tan, a pointy snout, tall leathery ears, small beady eyes, sturdy clawed feet and a long armoured tail tapering to a point. A sprinkle of coarse pale hairs pokes out between the bands.
reasoning:
I'm sketching the proportions for a realistic armadillo model in a trotting pose—working out body length, tail length, and shoulder height based on typical nine-banded armadillo dimensions.

I'm reviewing the SDK's available builder methods and paint helpers so I use only valid function names when constructing the geometry, then settling on a dusty pinkish-tan color palette with darker banding for the shell.

I'm now mapping out the armadillo's pose, setting the spine as a catmull curve from shoulders to hips with the body modeled as a loft along that bone chain, and planning to use stripes to create the segmented shell bands.

For the head, I'm setting up a neck chain running from the shoulder joint up to a head/snout tip, keeping the rig simple with just a couple of named joints.

I'll build the spine using a root hips joint and a catmull-rom chain of two spans connecting hips to shoulders, then work out a similar short chain for the neck.

Still working out the limb structure — defining front and back legs with shoulder/hip anchors, foot targets near ground level, and bone lengths for the upper and lower segments.

Parenting the limb roots to the last spine joint should work fine. I'm figuring out actual coordinates: shoulder and hip root positions, foot target positions, and limb segment lengths so the reach distances stay under the max extension, then setting up a trotting gait where diagonal leg pairs move forward and back together.

Writing limb/bend configuration...

For the claws, I'll position the spike base near the front of the paw with a direction angled forward and downward, attaching it to the paw joint so it inherits the bone's orientation, then loop to create multiple claws spread slightly apart.

Now I'm planning the head and neck: a chain of joints going from shoulder to a head joint at the tip, then building the skull as a tapered sweep along a separate path to get a pointed snout look, with the head attached to that final joint.

I'm roughly sizing the head placement relative to the body so the overall proportions match a nine-banded armadillo, with the body and tail totaling about 0.6m.

Now I'm working out the ears: tall leathery leaf shapes extruded flat against the head, positioned using local offsets so they mirror correctly on left and right, oriented to lie in the plane facing outward with a tapered, slightly backward-tilted leaf outline.

For the eyes I'm placing small dark spheres near the head joint, working through the lateral offset math so they sit on the surface of the head's tapering sweep rather than floating inside or outside it.

I decide to simplify by using a surface-nearest approach: wrap the head sweep as a surface, find the nearest point to an approximate eye location, and stick a tiny sphere there embedded partially into the mesh so it reads as a seated eye. I'm planning to reuse the same surface-nearest trick for placing the ear bases onto the head.

Still writing extrude params...

I'm now sketching the body shell as a loft over a sequence of spine stations, each with a position, width, and height, tapering from a narrower rear to a fuller front torso.

For the skeleton, I'm defining a hips joint as the spine root, then building a short spine chain up toward the shoulders, and a separate tail chain curving backward and downward with tapering thickness. I'm planning to apply banded armor coloring along the tail using periodic stripe patterns.

For the body surface, I'm scattering small hair spikes across it using random sampling with a minimum distance constraint, generating each as a tiny thin cone pointing outward from the surface normal to mimic coarse pale hairs poking between the armor bands.

I'm thinking around 60-70 hairs is plenty, filtering out most on the lower belly where there'd naturally be fewer. For the shell pattern, I want to layer fine stripe banding with a countershading effect that lightens the belly region, and I'll use a dusty pinkish-tan tone for the legs and a darker pink for the snout/nose area, plus a small sphere part for the nose tip.

Working out the snout attachment point using the head joint's local forward offset, placing it close to where the neck chain terminates near the head tip, and noting that ears sit on top with small eyes nearby. The pose stays in a neutral trot stance, and I'm structuring the module to export a build function returning the root along with name/description metadata, with hair spikes inheriting color from whatever surface they're placed on.

Now I'm tracing through the spine and neck joint hierarchy to make sure the neck chain parents correctly off the upper spine joint and that the positions along the catmull path line up properly between the shoulder point and the base of the neck.

I'm defining the head sweep geometry with a rigid bone binding and a radius taper from a wider base near the neck to a narrow point at the snout tip to create a cone-like pointed shape.

For the eyes, I'm finding the nearest surface point on the head sweep near the upper-front region to place them symmetrically. For the ears, I'm positioning them at the top-back of the head, extruding a tall leathery outline standing upright on the head's side plane so they read as proper ears from the side.

Now I'm shaping the tail as a bone chain tapering from the hips to a sharp point, using a sweep with linearly decreasing radius and point-end caps, then applying a banded tan/dark stripe paint along its length. For the main body, I'm setting up a loft bound to the spine bone with stations defining width and height to form the shield-like shoulder and hip regions.

I'm placing the leg roots partially inside the body's edge so the limbs attach naturally below the shoulder and hip shields, with front legs parented to the mid-spine joint and hind legs parented to the hip root.

For each leg I'm generating an IK chain between root and target points, naming joints by side (shoulderL/elbowL/pawL, etc.) and checking that reach distances stay under the limb's max extension. I'm sweeping each leg chain with a tapering radius for the limb silhouette, then adding a few claw spikes at the paw tips without binding them to a specific bone, since the nearest-joint fallback should land on the paw anyway.

I'm scattering small hair spikes across the body's surface using a filtered sample so they avoid the underside, then placing the eyes and nose by querying the head surface and offsetting along the head joint's local forward axis. For the shell I'm applying a banded stripe paint with a countershaded belly tint, and giving the tail and head their own flat-ish variants of the same palette.

Now I'm assembling the actual build function: creating the builder, defining the hips as root joint, lofting the spine through catmull-interpolated station points, branching off a tail chain and a neck-to-head chain, then looping over both sides to construct front and hind limb chains with their sweeps and claws, and finally lofting the body shell geometry over the spine stations with the banded paint applied.

I'm defining the ear outline as a thin extruded shape anchored near the top of the head, sized and positioned so its base sits just within the head surface, and tilted back slightly along the forward axis. For the eyes I'm locating surface hits near the expected eye position and embedding small dark spheres there, while the nose is a small sphere offset forward and slightly downward from the head joint's local frame.

I'm building the tail chain with three joints tapering off from the hips, sweeping it to a pointed tip using the same banded paint as the shell, then scattering hair spikes across the body surface using a y-normal filter to keep them off the belly. After double-checking that all the limb and loft calls use properly typed options and that nothing references an undefined variable, I return the finished root to close out the build function.
